title: Strategy benchmarking on recorded queries (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each candidate strategy runs over the recorded query log, and success is measured by the same engagement-based metric the history analyzer uses. Benchmarking on real recorded queries keeps the comparison grounded in actual user needs. Strategies are compared on identical query sets so the contest is fair. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
log = ['index latency', 'hash verify', 'posting lists']
strategies = {'keyword': 0.72, 'semantic': 0.81, 'hybrid': 0.88}
print('benchmark scores:', strategies)
print('leader:', max(strategies, key=strategies.get))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Search Strategy Optimizer, 2026-10-21.

title: Parameter tuning by grid search (foundational)
description: Signature original: A strategy's parameters, such as top-k cutoff or similarity threshold, are tuned with grid search over the recorded queries. Each grid point is scored on the full log, and the best point becomes the new default. Grid search is exhaustive over a small, sensible grid, which keeps tuning cheap and reproducible. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
best, best_s = None, -1
for k in [5, 10, 20]:
    score = 0.9 - abs(k - 10) * 0.01  # simulated measurement
    if score > best_s: best, best_s = k, score
print('tuned top_k:', best, 'score:', round(best_s, 3))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Search Strategy Optimizer, 2026-10-21.

title: Hybrid strategy composition search (foundational)
description: Signature original: The optimizer tries combining strategies, such as keyword retrieval with semantic reranking, and measures whether the hybrid beats its parts. Composition search tries a small set of known-good patterns rather than exploring blindly. A hybrid must beat the best single strategy by a margin to justify its complexity. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
single, hybrid = 0.81, 0.88
MARGIN = 0.03
print('hybrid gain:', round(hybrid - single, 2), '-> ADOPT' if hybrid - single >= MARGIN else '-> keep single')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Search Strategy Optimizer, 2026-10-21.

title: Metric-driven strategy selection (foundational)
description: Signature original: Selection optimizes a declared metric, such as engaged-result rate, never a vague notion of 'better'. The metric is fixed before benchmarking starts so the optimizer cannot shop for a flattering measure after seeing results. Metric discipline is what makes the optimization trustworthy. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
metric = 'engaged-result rate'
cands = {'keyword': 0.72, 'hybrid': 0.88}
print(f'selected on {metric}:', max(cands, key=cands.get))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Search Strategy Optimizer, 2026-10-21.

title: Rollout monitoring with guardrails (foundational)
description: Signature original: The winning strategy rolls out gradually with live monitoring of the same metric, and guardrails trigger rollback if the metric drops. Rollout monitoring catches the gap between benchmark and production that offline testing can miss. Every rollout decision is logged with its metric evidence. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
